trinidad-and-tobago.title: Flag of the Republic of Trinidad and Tobago

colors.note: Background field; represents the vitality of the land, warmth, and courage of the people.
Two parallel borders around the black diagonal; represents the sea, purity, and equality.
Diagonal band running from upper hoist to lower fly; represents the dedication of the people and shared wealth of the land.

desc:
- A red field with a black diagonal band bordered by two white stripes, running from the upper hoist to the lower fly
- Designed by Carlisle Chang, a noted Trinidadian painter, as part of an independence committee
- Adopted on 31 August 1962, the day of independence from the United Kingdom
trivia:
- The three colours red, white, and black are said to represent fire, water, and earth, the elements of life
- The diagonal band symbolises the equality and solidarity of all citizens regardless of origin
- Designer Carlisle Chang was one of Trinidad and Tobago's most prominent visual artists and also contributed to the design of the national coat of arms
